title: Release gate count drift: a capture merged behind the release branch stales the grounding block
observation: Two branches that each capture one record regenerate the very same "N+1" counts line in the grounding docs; the forge merges identical lines with no conflict, the merged store holds N+2, and the committed CLAUDE.md is one behind — no hook ran, nobody erred. v1.26.2's first tagged run (219 !== 220), PR #128 and PR #135 were all this lag, each fixed by a manual regenerate + retag. Resolved in 01084b1: the freshness test is direction-aware (src/core/groundingLag.ts) — a difference confined to the counts sentence where no append-only count exceeds the store is LAG, reported as a diagnostic and never red; an append-only count AHEAD of the store (a record never committed, fnd_6391b4242f) or divergent prose still fails. `hunch grounding` names the per-doc verdict and delta and `--refresh` regenerates from the PUBLIC store; `hunch init` installs a post-merge hook that refreshes after a local merge/pull that brought .hunch/ in.
evidence: test/grounding-merge-lag.test.ts: two branches each capture, identical count lines merge silently, hunch grounding reports `counts lag the store (decisions 2 → 3)` at exit 0, a doc AHEAD (4 → 3) exits 1, --refresh heals, the post-merge hook re-syncs a local merge
